rationale.consistency: Follows surrounding idioms: same lock-step compare via url.PathUnescape, EqualFold case-insensitivity, doc comment mirrors trimPathPrefix's; (int, bool) return is idiomatic Go.
rationale.edge_cases: Handles decoded pattern vs %2F/%62 path, escaped pattern requiring literal escape, upper/lower hex, invalid %zz treated as literal byte, empty suffix, non-matching suffix; end-anchoring check prevents mid-path matches.
rationale.scope: Only touches suffix path; extracting matchPathPrefix is a justified refactor to share logic and keeps prefix behaviour identical; removes now-dead reverse(). No unrelated edits.
rationale.readability: Clear names and a good contract comment on trimPathSuffix; pathBoundaries has no comment explaining why %xx triples are skipped, and the boundary-scan loop is a little dense.
rationale.robustness: No panic paths: bounds checked before slicing, unescape errors fall back to no-match/literal byte. Per-request slice allocation and O(n*m) scan are acceptable for path lengths but not tight.
rationale.maintainability: Prefix and suffix share one matcher, so contract changes land in one place; minor duplication of escape-skipping logic between pathBoundaries and matchPathPrefix.
